overview: S0B is the server-to-client animation broadcast, and the swing type (0) is the only animation a player emits at click rate, which makes it the one reliable signal that another player is attacking. Server-side anticheats cannot read the client's own swing inside S0B because it is outbound, so the swing checks in this corpus consume the inbound arm-animation packet (C0A, PacketPlayInArmAnimation) that the client sends on every left click, plus the outbound S0B on the few checks that listen on the send side. The corpus splits into no-swing validators (NCP fight NoSwing, Grim NoSwingBreak, ThotPatrol NoSwingA, MIU NoSwing), autoclicker statistics over the swing stream (Frequency AutoClickerA, Hydro AutoClickerA-D, Kauri AutoclickerA-D, Artemis AutoClickerA-M, Salmon SwingA), and packet-order rules that demand a swing after every attack (Grim Post and PacketOrderB, Photon PacketAnalysisAnimation, Truthful PacketOrderA/D).

checks.name: NoSwing (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: Require an arm swing between attacks so that damage without the arm-animation packet is flagged.
checks.how_it_works: FightListener invokes check() on the Bukkit PlayerAnimationEvent that mirrors the inbound arm-animation packet. A counter increments per attack: when a swing arrives first, the violation level decays by a factor of 0.9; when an attack arrives without a swing, 1 violation level is added and the configured actions run, cancelling the attack once the threshold is crossed.
checks.detects: Killaura and no-swing modules that attack without sending the arm animation.
checks.variations: NCP repeats the same check for blockbreak and blockplace; Arc (Vrekt-Arc) generalizes it as AbstractBlockNoSwingCheck plus a combat NoSwing and a network-level SwingFrequency; MIU ships NoSwing and NoSwingA; ThotPatrol NoSwingA counts swings between attacks; Intave folds swing order into combat heuristics (NoSwingHeuristic, PacketOrderSwingHeuristic).

checks.name: NoSwingBreak (Grim)
checks.purpose: Verify that a swing animation accompanies block digging, flagging diggers that never swing.
checks.how_it_works: Registers as both a BlockBreakListener and a PreViaPacketReceiveListener. onBlockBreak sets sentBreak for any dig action that is not a cancel; onPreViaPacketReceive sets sentAnimation when Play.Client.ANIMATION arrives; on the next tick packet the check flags if a break was recorded without an animation. Both flags reset every tick, so the swing must land inside the same tick as the dig start. The check is marked experimental.
checks.detects: Nuker and fast-break modules that dig while suppressing the swing packet.
checks.variations: Grim Post enforces the swing-before-attack order with transaction timing; amnoah-BetterAnticheat ships the same pairing as NoSwingDigCheck and NoSwingCombatCheck; freppp-ThotPatrol NoSwingA is the compact 1.8 form.

checks.name: AutoClickerA (Frequency)
checks.purpose: Statistical autoclicker check over the arm-animation stream: human click timing must vary.
checks.how_it_works: PacketCheck on WrappedPlayInArmAnimation: while CPS is above 6.5 and the player is not digging or placing, the number of movement packets between swings is sampled. After 20 samples the check computes the standard deviation and the outlier count; a deviation below 2 with fewer than 2 outliers fails. Constant-interval autoclickers produce near-zero variance and trip the check.
checks.variations: Hydro AutoClickerA-D, Kauri AutoclickerA-D, Artemis AutoClickerA-M, Azure AutoClickerA and Salmon SwingA implement the same swing-interval statistics on their own event buses; Intave ClickPatterns runs the same idea through entropy and deviation click-pattern checks.

checks.name: PacketAnalysisAnimation (Photon)
checks.purpose: Enforce the client's own attack sequence: an arm animation must directly follow an attack.
checks.how_it_works: Listens to INTERACT_ENTITY and ANIMATION at LOW priority. An attack on an entity sets a packetAnalysisAnimationExpected flag; the next ANIMATION clears it; if another attack arrives while the flag is still set, the previous attack never produced a swing and the module flags with +30 violation level under a decaying violation management. Disabled on 1.8 servers, where ViaVersion reorders animations.
checks.detects: Killaura that sends attack packets without the swing the vanilla client always sends after a left click.
checks.variations: Grim Post enforces the same attack-then-swing order with transaction-based timing; Truthful PacketOrderA/D and Grim PacketOrderB flag the same ordering violation from different packet sets; Tecnio-AntiHaxerman ProtocolC/ProtocolE cover arm-animation protocol oddities.

checks.name: Post (Grim)
checks.purpose: Verify that action packets arrive inside the expected movement tick, and consume the outbound S0B swing to exempt injected animations.
checks.how_it_works: On the send side, WrapperPlayServerEntityAnimation (the S0B packet) for the player's own entity id records the current transaction when the type is SWING_MAIN_ARM or SWING_OFF_HAND. On the receive side, action packets (attack, dig, place, animation, interact) that arrive after a flying packet are queued, and a transaction boundary with queued packets flags a post violation through the prediction pipeline. The swing exemption keeps ViaVersion-injected animations from falsing the check.
checks.detects: Post packets sent after movement, which blink and timer modules produce; the swing-exemption path keeps legitimately injected animations from falsing.
checks.variations: Grim PacketOrderB and Photon PacketAnalysisAnimation cover related ordering rules; Truthful PacketOrderA/D run the same order checks on Truthful's listener.
